item.description:
The Tags panel gains editing and sorting, the command line prints your own playbook under each help page, and Settings remembers the folders this Mac has used as its shelf.
### What's new
- Right-click a tag in the Tags panel and choose Edit Tag… to give it a meaning, rename, merge or remove it, without leaving where you are (SED-114). - Sort the Tags panel by Name or by Count with the two buttons at its top, to see which tags carry the shelf; the window keeps the choice until you close it (SED-115). - Bind a playbook folder in Settings ▸ Command Line Tool, and the command line prints your own markdown under each help page: ADD.md under sediment help add, TAGS.md under sediment help tags. sediment help playbook explains it (SED-117). - Settings ▸ Shelf Folder lists the last 3 folders this Mac used as its shelf under Recent Shelf Folders: Use Folder… switches back to one after asking in the shelf window, and Forget takes one off the list. A folder that is no longer on this Mac says so (SED-119).
### Changed
- The Tags panel's second line reads the right way round: a tag's meaning is the stronger grey, *No meaning yet* the lighter one, and a tag only one artifact carries is no longer marked in amber (SED-114). - sediment help tags no longer carries one operator's tag conventions; they are the example on sediment help playbook (SED-117). - Sediment can now write one folder outside its container, ~/Library/Application Support/Sediment/, to record the playbook binding for the command line (SED-117).
### Fixed
- Settings ▸ Support’s message box is set at the same size as the rows around it, where before its text and placeholder read a point larger (SED-116).

A Support tab writes your feedback as an email in your own mail app, Suggestions walk a dated series one issue at a time, and the themes gain Nocturne while Verdigris takes a coral accent.
### What's new
- Settings ▸ Support writes an email to the developer: choose what it's about, write your message, and choose whether to attach a diagnostic report. The report carries no personal information. Write Email… opens the draft in your own mail app, so you see everything before you send it; Sediment itself sends nothing. Help ▸ Send Feedback… opens the tab (SED-112).
### Changed
- Suggestions walk a series one issue at a time: the eight listed are the ones nearest this artifact by creation date, its own series first, newest at the top, and each row shows when its artifact was created and last modified (SED-110). - A click on a suggestion is now a step of the walk, as J and K are: the row stays marked, the list holds still, and ⎋ returns to the origin. A click on the origin's row steps back to it and the walk goes on. ↩ starts the walk on the origin's row when it is shown, so nothing changes until the first J (SED-110). - The artifact Suggestions is about is called the origin everywhere: its row reads *Origin*, the setting is *Show the origin at the top of Suggestions*, and ⎋'s hint is *Back to origin* (SED-110). - Tab and section headers read in Title Case: Settings' Shelf Folder tab, This Shelf, Command Line Tool and Menu Bar, and the Devices tab's Not Caught Up and Up to Date groups. The command line's relink hint names Settings ▸ Command Line Tool to match (SED-111). - Settings ▸ Appearance ▸ Theme reads Strata, Verdigris, Nocturne, Shale, Graphite and Flint. Verdigris keeps its cream and deep teal under a coral accent, and Nocturne is new: Dracula's night, with a cyan button. Lichen is retired; if you were using it, Sediment now shows Strata (SED-113).
### Fixed
- Clicking a control in Settings, such as a theme under Appearance, no longer leaves a focus ring around it. The ring shows only when you move there with ⇥ or the arrow keys (SED-112). - The diagnostic report no longer carries the names your sync provider gives its conflict copies of Sediment's own files, which can include a person's or a Mac's name (SED-112).

Tags grow into a vocabulary the shelf owns. An agent tags an artifact from the command line in one call, each tag can carry a meaning that travels with the shelf, a tag is edited from inside its collection, the Tags tab shows what is still untagged, and a shelf can require a tag of everything the command line adds.
### What's new
- From the command line, `sediment add` takes `--description` and `--tag`, so an agent files a tagged artifact in one call; `sediment update --tag` and `--untag` add or remove a tag without rewriting the description, and the reply says which tags are new to the shelf (SED-97). - `sediment tags` prints every tag in use with its count, and `sediment find --untagged` lists the artifacts carrying none (SED-97). - Each tag can carry a one-line meaning, kept in the shelf folder and shared with every Mac. `sediment tags describe` writes one and `sediment tags` shows them; the Tags tab shows each meaning under its tag, says *No meaning yet* where there is none, and tints a tag only one artifact carries; Go to…'s `#` reaches a described tag even when nothing carries it (SED-97). - Inside a tag's collection, Edit Tag… (⌥⌘T) gives the tag a meaning, renames it on every artifact, merges it into another tag, or removes it from all of them, each in one step with one ⌘Z, which the toast names; a merge and a removal ask first, and a rename to a name already in use points you at Merge into…. A collection nothing carries says how to leave it or edit its tag (SED-97). - The Suggestions tab lists the artifact you’re reading above the ones like it, marked when a walk brings you back to it with K; you can turn this off in Settings ▸ General ▸ Artifacts. - The Tags tab's first row, Untagged, opens the artifacts carrying no tag, so the ones `sediment find --untagged` lists are one click away (SED-108). - Settings ▸ General ▸ This shelf can require a tag from the command line: with it on, an agent’s `sediment add` or `update` that would leave an artifact untagged is refused and told to pass `--tag`. The setting travels with the shelf, and `sediment shelf` reports it (SED-109).
### Changed
- A tag an agent introduces from the command line is a line in Activity. - Show and hide the sidebar with ⌘B. ⌃⌘S no longer does anything.
### Fixed
- Closing Info during a Suggestions walk leaves the keyboard on the page, so the arrows keep scrolling it instead of moving the sidebar and ending the walk. - In Settings ▸ Appearance, VoiceOver now names the theme you are on as you move through the thumbnails with ⇥ or the arrow keys, where before it named Flint whichever theme was chosen.
